ordered_diagnoses: Prostatic Stromal Tumor of Uncertain Malignant Potential

facts.raw_span: 1 week of difficulty voiding
was catheterized for urinary retention
a large prostatic mass
prostate-specific antigen level was 0.62 ng/mL
he denied pain, fever, or abdominal distension
Physical examination was unremarkable
complete blood count, routine chemistries, and tumor markers (CEA, CA19-9, CA-125, SCC antigen, CYFRA) were all within normal limits
an enlarged prostate with palpable nodules and an ill-defined border
a 5.5-cm heterogeneous lesion in the right prostate lobe
cystoscopy raised suspicion for bladder invasion
Positron emission tomography–CT and colonoscopy suggested rectal invasion
prostatic stromal sarcoma or prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential

concepts.why: The patient's presentation with a large prostatic mass, urinary retention, and a heterogeneous lesion in the right prostate lobe, along with the biopsy result indicating prostatic stromal sarcoma or prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential, supports this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Prostatic Stromal Tumor of Uncertain Malignant Potential
concepts.why: The biopsy result indicating prostatic stromal sarcoma or prostatic stromal tumor of uncertain malignant potential, along with the patient's presentation with a large prostatic mass and a heterogeneous lesion in the right prostate lobe, supports this diagnosis as a possible alternative to prostatic stromal sarcoma.

The patient's presentation with a large prostatic mass and a heterogeneous lesion in the right prostate lobe could also be consistent with prostate cancer, although the biopsy result and other findings suggest a stromal tumor or sarcoma as more likely.
